text:
ali: Heads-up — starting the console cutover to strict fn/tool schema checks in the next prod deploy. Expect some fncall/toolhook rejects to bubble up. @maria can you watch the dashboard?

maria: On it. Which metric should I correlate with quota spikes? sampling or raw reject count?

ali: Raw rejects first (fncall.validation.rejects) + route tag. If rejects>1% of traffic for a route, open a ticket. Also watch `route_variant` tag (canary vs default).

jon: FYI some third-party adapters return arrays for `result` (legacy). Strict mode will reject those. We need a temporary coercion layer or route fallback.

kate: Can we auto-route rejects to permissive variant that coerces arrays -> object `{ items: [...] }`? That would avoid user-facing 500s.

ali: Proposal: on reject, route to `permissive-model-variant` for the same customer for N=3 attempts, then fallback to legacy `degen` route. Need to tie to quota/cost so we don't double-bill.

sam: We should expose that behavior in the console: "reject -> permissive reroute" toggle per-project. PM wants explicit UX.

maria: Building a small dashboard tile now: chart fncall.validation.rejects (1m) by route and `route_variant`. Also add sample payloads list. Will send link when ready.

jon: Example payload that keeps failing:
```json
{
  "tool": "pricing_fetch",
  "output": [
    { "price": 9 },
    { "price": 12 }
  ]
}
```
This should be valid but our schema expects `output` to be an object with `entries`.

kate: Can we add a lightweight adapter in the gateway that attempts simple coercions before rejecting? e.g., if array -> wrap in `{ entries: array }`. Low CPU.

ali: Yes but need telemetry flags to know which coercions were applied. We should tag coerced responses with `validation.coerced=true` and include `validation.coercion_type=wrap_array`. That helps audits.

sre-bot: Deploy scheduled: prod/dreamland at 12:15 UTC — will run migration that enables strict-schema gate on 10% canary.

maria: Dashboard link: https://internal.redwood/boards/fncall-rejects?canary=10% — added sample table + last 50 payloads (redacted).

jon: Also seeing a spike in fncall.latency for routes that hit the adapter; coercion adds ~12ms. Fine but call it out.

sam: UX ask: show "policy applied" toast when we reroute, with a link to why it happened + sample. PM wants to reduce support tickets.

kate: About billing: reroutes consume extra token units — ops wants a cap per-customer to avoid runaway cost. Maybe a soft cap: after 5 reroutes in 1h for a route, disable automatic reroutes for that customer and surface a warning.

ali: Agree. Add metric `validation.reroutes.count` per customer. If count>5 in 1h emit alert and set project flag `reroutes_blocked=true`.

maria: I'll add an alert rule and a console banner to explain. Also will log `validation.rejection_sample_id` so support can fetch the exact sample.

jon: Quick checklist before canary: 1) coercion adapter PR + rollout flag 2) dashboard tile 3) alert rule 4) console UX toggle 5) billing soft-cap 6) telemetry tags included 

ali: Correct. Anyone volunteering to own rollback playbook? Need steps to revert to permissive default if we get noisy.

kate: I'll own rollback. Playbook draft: 
- disable strict gate feature flag
- flip canary to 0%
- clear `reroutes_blocked` flags
- run postmortem if >0.5% user-facing 500s

maria: Putting all this into a runbook doc. Slack will get updates.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started (10%) — prod/dreamland at 12:15 UTC.

jon: Picking 2 customers to watch manually: cust-omega, cust-lumen — they have heavy legacy adapters.

ali: Ok let's reconvene in 30m. Ping here with any emergent rejects that need immediate ACLing. :thumbsup:

maria: Noted. If we see false positives, I'll flip coercion to `on` for that customer and annotate the alert.

kate: Thanks team.

ali: Closing — thanks.
